facts.text: Fenton’s first settlers arrived in the mid‑1830s, just after the Black Hawk War cleared the region of Native tribes.
The village was named for Joseph Fenton, the New Jersey pioneer who settled there in October 1835.
Fenton sits beside the Rock River, a major Mississippi tributary whose ancient meltwater carved the surrounding valley.
Early settlers trekked by canal boat to Buffalo, schooner to Chicago, then ox‑wagon to Dixon’s Ferry before claiming a 215‑acre homestead near the Rock River.
Fenton township was formally organized in 1852, briefly eyed the name Eden, and by 1877 boasted about 1,000 farmers linked by rail.
Today, Fenton remains an unincorporated rural community that relies on agriculture and landmarks such as the 1870‑built New Lebanon Church.
